e-8553.worked_solution:
If $X \sim \textrm{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069741/assets/5973b712a92cadd7bc301f7e8e859a1a53a551cfeee0b0ac1404ddbfc352ac56.png)

Here, $X \sim \textrm{Geom}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069741/assets/a7c5af2adc67390439a5d46933083b796c30fc55f0f1f5ff8cd9d374a905695d.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=3) & =f(3) \\  & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{3}{4}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x-1}(\frac{3}{4}), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=3) & =f(3) \\  & ={(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}(\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability at a Point
content.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(0.15),$ compute $P(X=7).$  Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
content.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.15),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{(0.85)}^{x-1}(0.15), & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=7) & =f(7) \\  & ={(0.85)}^{6}(0.15) \\  & ≈0.0566.\end{aligned}
$$
